submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires on the word that opens a noun or verb complement right after a scope/locative or predicate head: mainly the determiner after locative 'in' (' the', ' a', ' an'; French ' la'/' une' after 'dans'/'en'), e.g. 'in the United States', 'in the world', 'in the house' (about 0.4-1.0 x max), weaker after 'into'/'over'/'on' (about 0.3-0.5), and a rate/degree adverb or participle right after a copula or 'a' in a clause about change ('is rapidly', 'is increasingly', 'is quickly', 'a growing', 'an infinite', about 0.6-0.9). Predicted inactive (below 0.25 x max, measured 16 of 20 plain sentences plus all 'at the' edits): English sentences of at most 12 tokens with no copula (is/are/was) and whose determiners follow only a verb or 'at', 'to', 'with', 'under', 'of', 'for' (e.g. 'We ate dinner at the restaurant.', 'He read the letter twice.', where only the final period reaches about 0.18), and code or number lists (about 0); outside that class are 'in/into/over/on/dans + determiner' and 'copula + adverb or adjective'.

Among the many challenges facing the Parks & Recreation industry, climate change and competition for resources are at the forefront for 2018. Due to changing climate, the parks and rec industry must account and plan for the extreme weather that comes along with it, such as extreme heat and cold, rain and thunderstorms and events like tornadoes or hurricanes. Changing climate has changed the planning, design and management of parks, facilities, and public land. Along with climate change, increased competition for land and funding has affected the parks and recreation industry.
Sufficient and sustainable funding is hard to come by, and the lack of adequate funding hinders new opportunities, innovative solutions and often times facilities are poorly maintained and unsafe. As a result of these issues becoming more prevalent, sustainability initiatives have been adapted by many companies to help combat these concerns.
In a recent report from the National Recreation and Park Association (NRPA), light is shed on how companies and parks and recreation agencies are integrating these practices into their daily routine. Among the numerous sustainability initiatives included in the report, many pertain to environmentally-friendly products and procedures that are easy to implement.
Initiatives to help conserve natural resources have been put in place. Some of these initiatives include reducing landfill waste, protecting wildlife and providing community education. Another sustainability initiative that is increasingly being adopted is to use environmentally-friendly building practices. The report states that 43% of companies are using recycled construction materials.
Using recycled construction material for parks and rec products is a great way to help conserve natural resources. It also keeps waste out of the landfills and is a sustainable building solution that is built to last with low maintenance cost and effort.
Although traditional wood is a common building material for many parks and recreation projects, a better alternative in many circumstances is structural recycled plastic lumber. Not only is it durable and strong, it also is well suited for outdoor applications where structural support or load bearing is required.
Besides its structural integrity, plastic lumber doesn’t require painting or staining and will not rot or splinter. Many times graffiti can become an unwanted addition to playground equipment, and with plastic lumber, the paint will not adhere and can be easily washed off. This environmentally-friendly product cuts, drills and secures like traditional wood and can increase profitability over time because it is built to last and has a 50 year warranty.

“I'll be perfectly honest, for one,” he said. “I thought and still think that she looked upon me as a friendly juror. Nothing wrong about it, mind you--not a thing. I wouldn't have you think that she deliberately--er--ahem! What have you to say, No. 7?”

No. 7 blushed violently. “Not a word,” said he. “I profess to be a gentleman.”

No. 8 snorted. “Well, then, act like one. Mr. Sampson's a gentleman. He don't hesitate to say that he was--Say, Mr. Sampson, just what did you say?”

“I said, without the slightest desire to create a wrong impression, that I was deeply affected by the trust Miss Hildebrand appeared to place in me. She believes her grandfather to be innocent, and I think she believes that I agree with her. That's the long and the short of it.” No. 4 slammed his fist upon the table. “By thunder, that's just exactly the fix I'm in. Right from the start, I seemed to feel that I got on this jury because she liked the looks of me. Not the way you think, Hooper, but because I looked like a man who might give her grandfather a square trial and--”

Mr. Hooper interrupted him hotly: “What do you mean by 'not the way you think'? That sounded kind of disparaging, my good man--disparaging to her. Explain yourself.” Sampson interposed. “I think we all understand each other, gentlemen. Miss Hildebrand practically picked the whole dozen of us. She inspected us as we came up, she sized us up, and she had the final word to say as to whether we were acceptable to the defence. She believed in us, or we wouldn't be here to-night. What makes it all the harder for us, gentlemen, individually and collectively, is that we believe in her. Now, what are we to do? Live up to her estimate of us, or live up to a prior estimate of ourselves?”

“Well, let's sleep over it,” said the foreman uneasily. “I guess we're all tired and--”

“I guess we won't sleep much,” broke in No. 7 miserably. “Damn' if you'll ever get me on a jury again. I'm a nervous man anyhow and now--I'm a wreck. I don't know what to do about this business.”

“If it were not for Miss Hildebrand, gentlemen, we'd all know what to do,” said Sampson. “Isn't that a fact?”

“Well, you seem to have made up your mind,” said No. 8 gloomily. “I thought mine was made up, but, by gosh, I--I want to do what's right. I took my oath to--”

“We will take a ballot before breakfast in the morning,” said No. 1 decisively. “Now, let's sleep if we can.”

They disposed themselves in chairs, stretched out their legs and--waited for an illuminating daybreak.

Sampson's decision was final. He would not stultify his honour. He would not be swayed by the sweetest emotion that ever had assailed him. Besides, he argued through the long, tedious hours before dawn, when all was said and done, what could Alexandra Hildebrand ever be to him? She would go out of his life the day that--

adversarial_test_results.detail: Mirrors top example 8 ('the modern industrial world'); hypothesis predicts inactive because 'the' follows 'by' with no locative in-head and no copula.

adversarial_test_results.detail: Same change topic as the claim but with no copula and no in/dans head; 'the' follows 'across', so the hypothesis predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The soup is dinner for the hungry kids tonight.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Copula followed by a noun ('is dinner'), not a rate/degree adverb or participle about change; 'the' follows 'for', so the hypothesis predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The answer is the Eiffel Tower in Paris.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Copula followed by a determiner ('is the') and 'in' followed by a proper noun with no determiner; neither trigger class is met, so the hypothesis predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: In principle we agreed to postpone the vote until June.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same trigger word 'In' in the fixed phrase 'in principle' with no determiner after it; 'the' follows a verb, so the hypothesis predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Come in and close the door behind you right now.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Part-of-speech switch: 'in' as a verb particle rather than a locative head, and 'the' follows the verb 'close'; the hypothesis predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The river rose rapidly after engineers opened the dam gates.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Claimed adverb 'rapidly' after an ordinary verb ('rose') with no copula; 'the' follows a verb, so the hypothesis predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Costs rose, and increasingly angry residents packed the town hall.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Claimed adverb 'increasingly' in attributive position before an adjective rather than after a copula; the hypothesis predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The child keeps growing out of shoes bought at the market.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Part-of-speech switch: 'growing' as a complement of 'keeps' rather than after a copula or 'a'; 'the' follows 'at', so the hypothesis predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: def total(xs): return sum(xs) # computed over list items
adversarial_test_results.detail: Code control from the hypothesis's stated inactive class; no determiner or copula triggers at all.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Nous voyageons dans Paris chaque printemps avec nos amis proches.
adversarial_test_results.detail: French near-miss: 'dans' followed by a proper noun with no determiner, so the dans-plus-determiner trigger is absent; the hypothesis predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Elle est en colere contre son frere depuis hier matin deja.
adversarial_test_results.detail: French near-miss: 'en' followed by a bare noun with no determiner; the en-plus-determiner trigger is absent, so the hypothesis predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The cat hid quietly under the porch during the thunderstorm.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Determiner follows 'under', an explicitly inactive preposition in the hypothesis; no copula and no in-head, so the hypothesis predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He painted the fence with the old brush from the shed.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Determiner follows 'with', an explicitly inactive preposition; 'old' is an adjective after a determiner rather than after a copula, so the hypothesis predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Mathematicians debated the infinite scope of prime numbers.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Part-of-speech switch: 'infinite' as an attributive adjective after 'the' rather than after a copula or 'a/an'; no in-head, so the hypothesis predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She left her keys in the kitchen drawer this morning.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel everyday locative 'in the' with a determiner opening the complement, the core claimed trigger, in a non-encyclopedic context.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They camped in a meadow beside the river for two nights.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel locative 'in a' opening a noun complement, the claimed trigger, with vocabulary absent from the top examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The rookie is rapidly improving his free throw percentage this season.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel copula-plus-'rapidly' change clause in a sports genre absent from the top examples, the claimed adverb trigger.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The software is increasingly unreliable after each recent automatic update.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel copula-plus-'increasingly' change clause in a tech genre absent from the top examples, paraphrasing the degree-adverb trigger.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He poured the mixture into the bowl and stirred it slowly.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel 'into the' complement opening, the claimed weaker trigger, in an everyday cooking context unlike the historical top examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Yeah, we keep the spare blankets in a closet down the hall.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Cross-genre holdout: dialogue-style 'in a' complement opening, the claimed trigger in ultrachat-like casual speech.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Ils ont passe tout l'hiver dans la vallee pres de Grenoble.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Cross-language holdout: French 'dans la' plus determiner opening a locative complement, the exact claimed French trigger.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She found shelter in an old barn during the storm.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel 'in an' plus adjective opening a noun complement, paraphrasing the claimed determiner trigger with unseen vocabulary.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The startup faces a growing shortage of engineers this quarter.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel 'a growing' change noun phrase in a business genre absent from the top examples, the claimed participle trigger.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They ran out of water and rested in the shade of a canyon.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Two-sentence holdout with the 'in the' trigger delayed into the second sentence, testing the retrospective long-range reading with novel vocabulary.
